ety.text: Latin sēmi-bor. English semi- English conductor English semiconductor From semi- + conductor.

senses.d: A substance with electrical properties intermediate between a good conductor and a good insulator.
ex: Integrated circuits are made from semiconductors, especially silicon.

grp.label: substance with electrical properties between conductor and insulator

ety.text: From German Semester, from New Latin sēmestris (“lasting six months”), from sex (“six”) + mēnsis (“month”).

senses.d: Half of a school year (US) or academic year such as autumn or spring semester.
ex: I will graduate at the end of the spring semester.

senses.d: A period or term of six months.

ety.text: From German Seminar, from Latin sēminārium, from sēmen (“seed”). Compare seminary.

senses.d: A class held for advanced studies in which students meet regularly to discuss original research, under the guidance of a professor.
ex: Students attended a seminar on climate change.
She gave a guest lecture during the philosophy seminar.

senses.d: A meeting held for the exchange of useful information by members of a common business community.
ex: The company hosted a training seminar for new employees.

senses.d: To participate in or lead a seminar.

grp.label: meeting held for the exchange of useful information
